newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA ON THE BRINK OF HYPERINFLATION - ECONOMISTS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA ON THE BRINK OF HYPERINFLATION - ECONOMISTS.

text.p: Bulgaria's plummetting lev may trigger hyperinflation in the short term as products sold locally have dollar components and prices are directly linked to the dollar rate, economists said on Tuesday.

"The lev/dollar rates and the movement of prices are such that we can assume Bulgaria is about to enter a hyperinflationary spiral," the head of the Economy Institute of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, Dimitar Dimitrov, told a news conference.
The lev which traded at 70 to the dollar in January hits new all-time lows each week. It closed at 515-520 to the dollar on Tuesday.
Most shops have posted signs "Prices plus 40 percent" to save them adjusting individual price tags.

Monthly inflation in the past seven months has averaged around 20 percent and dropped to 9.7 percent in November. The institute said that the government and the central bank had exhausted all measures to control price rises.
"It turned out that monetary instruments are no longer effective even in the short term," said the institute's deputy director Ivanka Kraininska.
"Stabilisation measures must be aimed at the real economy to cure the cause of the illness rather than the illness itself," said Kraininska.
Figures released by the National Statistics Institute on Tuesday put cumulative inflation for the first 11 months of 1996 at 223.6 percent.
Both Kraininska and Dimitrov said the lev could be stabilised only by boosting investment in production and establishing a favourable investment climate by speeding up privatisation.
Kraininska attributed the current financial crisis to seven years of delayed reform and privatisation.
Bulgaria is currently negotiating with the International Monetary Fund the introduction of a currency board regime to boost confidence in the lev and the crumbling financial system.
"There are circles in Bulgaria for whom hyperinflation is a convenient way to melt down the huge internal indebtedness," said Kraininska. She did not elaborate.
Payments on government securities due next year amount to 380 billion levs with the greater burden of maturities falling in January, February, August and November, said Kraininska.
The burden of these payments will fall on the population because under a currency board system central bank lending will be banned, she added.
Dimitrov saw this year's inflation at around 300 percent. Next year's inflation depended on what measures the government adopted before introducing the currency board system, he said.
